# statemachine

```go
import "github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/statemachine"
```

Package statemachine is a state-machine engine over stored entities (ADR 0120): declare the states an entity goes through and the transitions between them, hand the engine your store, and it moves entities along — on the events you fire, and by itself on timers, deadlines and guards.

```
def := statemachine.Define(func(o *Order) *Status { return &o.Status }).
    Initial(Pending).
    On("pay", Pending, Paid).
    After("abandon", 24*time.Hour, Pending, Cancelled).    // a duration in the state
    At("expire", Paid, Expired, func(o Order) (time.Time, bool) { return o.ShipBy, !o.ShipBy.IsZero() }).
    When("ready", Paid, Shipping, func(o Order) bool { return o.Packed }).
    OnEnter(Paid, chargeCard).                               // before the store: an error cancels
    OnTransition(publish)                                    // after the store: an error is reported

m, err := statemachine.New(ctx, def, &statemachine.Config[Order, Status]{
    Store: orders, Journal: records,
    Report: func(ctx context.Context, err error) { log.Print(err) }, // what no return value carries
})
go func() {
    if err := m.Run(ctx); err != nil {                       // LoopRunning: another loop is going
        log.Print(err)
    }
}()                                                          // fires timers, deadlines and guards
o, err := m.Start(ctx, Order{ID: "o-1"})                     // Pending, inserted
o, err = m.Fire(ctx, "o-1", "pay")                           // Paid, replaced
```

### Your store is the source of truth

The state is a field of your entity and the entity lives in your [Store](#Store): the engine reads it with Get, creates with Insert and moves with Replace — a Replace that finds the entity gone stores nothing, so a transition never brings back an entity deleted meanwhile. Beside the store the machine keeps one [Record](#Record) per entity — its state, since when, its latest transitions — in memory and in the [Journal](#Journal) you give it, which is what keeps an After timer counting across a restart. Tell the machine about writes it did not make with Machine.Changed and Machine.Deleted: a write can move a deadline or make a guard hold, and a state changed behind its back enters its record as of the moment the machine learns of it.

### Transitions

Transitions of one entity run one at a time, transitions of different entities concurrently. A transition runs the OnEnter hooks of the state entered, stores the entity, records the step, releases the entity and then runs the OnTransition hooks. A hook that panics fails what it was part of — an OnEnter hook its transition, an OnTransition hook only itself — and never leaves an entity locked. An OnEnter hook may change the entity but not its state or key, and must not fire its own machine (Reentrant); an OnTransition hook may.

### The loop never polls

Machine.Run keeps an agenda: each entity in a state a timer or a guard leaves has one entry, the instant its earliest automatic transition falls due, on a heap. The loop fires what is due — per entity, the first declared transition due — and sleeps until the next one or until a write wakes it, never sooner than Config.MinGap after its last run, so a burst of writes is one run. Finding the next transition due costs O(log N) where a loop that re-reads the store on every wake pays O(N); BENCH.md in the engine measures both. An entity whose transition fails is retried after Config.Backoff, counted per entity. Give the machine a clock.ManualClock (pkg/v1/clock) and a test drives every timer.

### What it does not do

It is not a durable workflow runtime: there is no replay, no activity, no compensation, and nothing survives a crash but what your store and your journal hold. A write to an entity that does not go through the machine can race with a transition of it; the store's Replace is the arbiter.

Initialised with `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/statemachine.WaitAbandoned`.

Code `0.3.88.20` · reason `WAIT_ABANDONED` · public "The request ended while the entity was busy"

<a name="Config"></a>
## type [Config](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/app/statemachine/facade_gen.go>)

Config parameterises New. Only Store is required.

```go
type Config[E any, S comparable] = svcstm.Config[E, S]
```

Config is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/app/statemachine.Config`, declared as:

```go
type Config[E any, S comparable] struct {
	// Store holds the entities. Required.
	Store      corestm.Store[E]
	// Journal keeps each entity's record beside the store. Nil keeps the
	// records in memory: after a restart every entity re-enters its state
	// when the machine opens, which restarts every After timer.
	Journal    corestm.Journal[S]
	// Clock is what the machine stamps and waits on. Nil is clock.System; a
	// clock.ManualClock drives every timer of a test.
	Clock      clock.Timed
	// Actor reads, from the context a caller hands Start or Fire, who fired
	// the transition; the result lands in the record's history and in the
	// change hooks receive. Never called for a transition the loop fires.
	// Nil records nobody.
	Actor      func(ctx context.Context) string
	// Observe brackets every transition the machine's OWN loop fires — the
	// ones no caller can wrap: it is called before the transition with the
	// loop's context, returns the context the transition's hooks and store
	// calls run under — a tracer puts its span there — and a function the
	// engine calls with the outcome once the OnTransition hooks have run and
	// the loop has recorded it: a panic there is reported as LoopPanicked and
	// changes nothing, the transition stands. A caller wraps its own Start and
	// Fire itself. It is called while the loop holds the entity, so it must
	// not fire that entity. Nil observes nothing.
	Observe    func(ctx context.Context, firing FiringValue[S]) (context.Context, func(err error))
	// Report receives every error no caller's return value carries: an
	// OnTransition hook's failure, a Journal write that failed, and each
	// transition the loop could not fire. It is called with no lock of the
	// machine held, so it may read the machine — its census, a record — or
	// fire it. Nil drops them — the SDK does not write to stderr on the
	// caller's behalf (ADR 0030) — so wire it.
	Report     func(ctx context.Context, err error)
	// OnLoop is told what Run does: a run starting, a run ending with what
	// it fired and when the loop wakes next, and the loop re-arming earlier
	// because a write arrived. Called on the loop's goroutine; keep it short.
	// Nil observes nothing.
	OnLoop     func(event LoopEvent)
	// MinGap is the least time between the end of one run of the loop and
	// the start of the next. Not positive means DefaultMinGap.
	MinGap     time.Duration
	// Backoff is how long an entity whose automatic transition failed waits
	// before it is tried again, by consecutive failures. A zero BaseDelay
	// means 1s doubling to a minute.
	Backoff    kbackoff.Value
	// MaxHistory is how many transitions each record keeps. Not positive
	// means DefaultMaxHistory.
	MaxHistory int
}
```

<a name="Definition"></a>
## type [Definition](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/app/statemachine/facade_gen.go>)

Definition declares a machine: its states, transitions and hooks.

```go
type Definition[E any, S comparable] = svcstm.MachineSpec[E, S]
```

Definition is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/app/statemachine.MachineSpec`, declared as:

```go
type Definition[E any, S comparable] struct{}
```

<a name="Definition.After"></a>
### func \(Definition\) [After](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/app/statemachine/definition.go>)

```go
func (*Definition) After(event string, delay time.Duration, from S, to S) *MachineSpec[E, S]
```

After declares a timer transition: an entity that has spent delay in state from moves to state to, fired by the machine's loop. The time is counted from when the entity entered the state, which the machine's journal keeps across restarts.

<a name="Definition.At"></a>
### func \(Definition\) [At](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/app/statemachine/definition.go>)

```go
func (*Definition) At(event string, from S, to S, instant func(E) (time.Time, bool)) *MachineSpec[E, S]
```

At declares a timer transition at an instant the entity carries: an entity in state from moves to state to once the instant instant returns has come; false means no instant for now. The engine asks again each time the entity is written, and its loop sleeps until the earliest instant.

<a name="Definition.Can"></a>
### func \(Definition\) [Can](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/app/statemachine/definition.go>)

```go
func (*Definition) Can(entity E, event string) bool
```

Can reports whether \[StateMachine.Fire] with event would move entity: an event transition by that name leaves its current state. It is a function of the declaration alone and needs no running machine.

<a name="Definition.Initial"></a>
### func \(Definition\) [Initial](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/app/statemachine/definition.go>)

```go
func (*Definition) Initial(state S) *MachineSpec[E, S]
```

Initial sets the state a new entity enters with \[StateMachine.Start]. A second call replaces the first.

<a name="Definition.InitialState"></a>
### func \(Definition\) [InitialState](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/app/statemachine/definition.go>)

```go
func (*Definition) InitialState() (state S, set bool)
```

InitialState returns the state a new entity enters, and whether Initial was called.

<a name="Definition.On"></a>
### func \(Definition\) [On](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/app/statemachine/definition.go>)

```go
func (*Definition) On(event string, from S, to S) *MachineSpec[E, S]
```

On declares an event transition: \[StateMachine.Fire] with event moves an entity in state from to state to. One event may leave several states, but only one transition per event and state.

<a name="Definition.OnEnter"></a>
### func \(Definition\) [OnEnter](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/app/statemachine/definition.go>)

```go
func (*Definition) OnEnter(state S, hook func(context.Context, *E) error) *MachineSpec[E, S]
```

OnEnter adds a hook run when an entity enters state, before it is stored. Hooks of one state run in declaration order.

An error cancels the transition, and so does a panic — recovered as \[corestm.HookPanicked], with the entity's lock released on the way out. A hook may change the entity but not its state nor its key (\[corestm.HookChangedState], \[corestm.HookChangedKey]), and must not fire its own machine: it runs under the entity's lock, so the call is refused with \[corestm.Reentrant] rather than waiting for itself.

<a name="Definition.OnTransition"></a>
### func \(Definition\) [OnTransition](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/app/statemachine/definition.go>)

```go
func (*Definition) OnTransition(hook func(context.Context, ChangeValue[E, S]) error) *MachineSpec[E, S]
```

OnTransition adds a hook run after every stored transition, whoever fired it — the natural place to publish it. Hooks run in declaration order, once the entity's lock is released, so a hook may fire the machine again. An error or a panic is reported through Config.Report; the transition stands and the next hooks still run.

<a name="Definition.Problems"></a>
### func \(Definition\) [Problems](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/app/statemachine/definition.go>)

```go
func (*Definition) Problems() []error
```

Problems returns the declaration's mistakes so far, in the order they were made, each an error carrying a code of this package and log-only fields naming the event, the state or the function concerned. A missing Initial is not among them — it is only a mistake once the declaration is complete, and NewStateMachine reports it as \[corestm.InitialMissing].

<a name="Definition.States"></a>
### func \(Definition\) [States](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/app/statemachine/definition.go>)

```go
func (*Definition) States() []S
```

States returns every state the declaration names, in the order each was first mentioned: the initial state, the ends of each transition, the states that have hooks.

<a name="Definition.Transitions"></a>
### func \(Definition\) [Transitions](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/app/statemachine/definition.go>)

```go
func (*Definition) Transitions() []TransitionValue[S]
```

Transitions returns the declared transitions in declaration order.

<a name="Definition.When"></a>
### func \(Definition\) [When](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/app/statemachine/definition.go>)

```go

```

When declares a guard transition: an entity in state from moves to state to as soon as guard holds. The guard sees the entity only and is asked each time the entity is written, never on a clock.

<a name="Machine"></a>
## type [Machine](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/app/statemachine/facade_gen.go>)

Machine runs a Definition over a Store. It is safe for concurrent use.

```go
type Machine[E any, S comparable] = svcstm.StateMachine[E, S]
```

Machine is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/app/statemachine.StateMachine`, declared as:

```go
type Machine[E any, S comparable] struct{}
```

<a name="Machine.Census"></a>
### func \(Machine\) [Census](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/app/statemachine/machine.go>)

```go
func (*Machine) Census() map[S]int
```

Census counts the entities per state. Every declared state is present, at zero when no entity is in it; an undeclared state found in the store is present while an entity is in it.

<a name="Machine.Changed"></a>
### func \(Machine\) [Changed](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/app/statemachine/notify.go>)

```go
func (*Machine) Changed(ctx context.Context, key string) error
```

Changed tells the machine the entity under key was written by something other than the machine — call it after the write is visible to Store.Get. The machine reads the entity: a state that changed behind its back enters its record as of now, and when a timer or a guard leaves the entity's state the loop is woken to ask again what is due — a write can move a deadline or make a guard hold. An entity the store no longer holds is forgotten, as by \[StateMachine.Deleted].

Calling it for the machine's own writes is harmless. When a transition of the entity is in flight — which is where a store that notifies on every write calls it from — it returns at once and the transition reads the entity again before it lets go of it. Call it OUTSIDE any lock of the store: it may wait for the entity's lock while the loop, holding it, reads the store.

<a name="Machine.Deleted"></a>
### func \(Machine\) [Deleted](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/app/statemachine/notify.go>)

```go
func (*Machine) Deleted(ctx context.Context, key string) error
```

Deleted tells the machine the entity under key was deleted: its record leaves the census, the journal and the agenda. A read or a transition of the entity in progress will not record it again. It returns the journal's failure, if any; the record is dropped either way.

<a name="Machine.Fire"></a>
### func \(Machine\) [Fire](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/app/statemachine/transition.go>)

```go
func (*Machine) Fire(ctx context.Context, key string, event string) (E, error)
```

Fire moves the entity under key along the event transition by that name leaving its current state, and returns it as stored.

It refuses a key the store does not hold (\[corestm.EntityMissing]), an event no transition takes from the entity's state (\[corestm.TransitionRefused] — returned with the entity, whose state says why), and a call made through the context an OnEnter hook of this machine was given (\[corestm.Reentrant]). On any other failure — a hook, the store — it returns the entity as it was read.

<a name="Machine.Record"></a>
### func \(Machine\) [Record](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/app/statemachine/machine.go>)

```go
func (*Machine) Record(key string) (corestm.RecordValue[S], bool)
```

Record returns what the machine keeps about the entity under key, and false when it knows none.

<a name="Machine.Records"></a>
### func \(Machine\) [Records](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/app/statemachine/machine.go>)

```go
func (*Machine) Records() []corestm.RecordValue[S]
```

Records returns every record, the most recently entered state first.

<a name="Machine.Run"></a>
### func \(Machine\) [Run](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/app/statemachine/loop.go>)

```go
func (*Machine) Run(ctx context.Context) error
```

Run is the machine's own loop: it fires the timer and guard transitions as they fall due, until ctx ends, and returns nil then. It returns \[corestm.LoopRunning] at once when another Run or a Step of this machine is going.

It never polls. A run fires what is due — per entity, the first declared transition due, one per entity per run — and the loop then sleeps until the next transition due or until a write wakes it: \[StateMachine.Changed], or a transition stored by Start or Fire. No run starts sooner than Config.MinGap after the previous one ended, so a burst of writes is one run. A machine with no timer and no guard never runs, and Run just waits for ctx.

An entity whose transition failed is tried again after Config.Backoff, counted per entity: one failing entity delays nobody else. Everything runs on the calling goroutine, so a caller's pprof labels cover every hook the loop runs.

<a name="Machine.Start"></a>
### func \(Machine\) [Start](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/app/statemachine/transition.go>)

```go
func (*Machine) Start(ctx context.Context, entity E) (E, error)
```

Start enters a new entity into the machine: it sets the initial state, runs the initial state's OnEnter hooks and inserts the entity, then runs the OnTransition hooks. The step recorded is core/app/statemachine.CreateEvent.

It returns the entity as stored. It refuses an entity whose key is empty (\[corestm.KeyEmpty]) or already taken (\[corestm.EntityExists]), and a call made through the context an OnEnter hook of this machine was given (\[corestm.Reentrant]).

<a name="Machine.Step"></a>
### func \(Machine\) [Step](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/app/statemachine/loop.go>)

```go
func (*Machine) Step(ctx context.Context) (time.Time, error)
```

Step makes one pass over what is due now: every entity written since the last pass is evaluated, and every entity whose transition is due fires it — the first declared one due, one transition per entity. It returns when the loop should look again by itself: the current instant when entities wait to be evaluated, the earliest due instant otherwise, the zero time when nothing is scheduled; and the failures joined.

It is for a caller that drives the machine itself instead of Run — a test, another scheduler. It returns \[corestm.LoopRunning] when Run or another Step is going.

### func \(Store\) [All](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/app/statemachine/design_gen.go>)

```

<a name="Store.Insert"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Insert](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/app/statemachine/design_gen.go>)

```

<a name="Store.Key"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Key](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/app/statemachine/design_gen.go>)

```go

```

<a name="Store.Replace"></a>

<a name="Transition"></a>
## type [Transition](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/app/statemachine/facade_gen.go>)

Transition is a declared transition, as Definition.Transitions reads it back.

```go
type Transition[S comparable] = svcstm.TransitionValue[S]
```

Transition is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/app/statemachine.TransitionValue`, declared as:

```go
type Transition[S comparable] struct {
	// Event is the transition's name.
	Event   string
	// From is the state it leaves.
	From    S
	// To is the state it enters.
	To      S
	// Trigger says how it fires: an event, a delay, a deadline or a guard.
	Trigger corestm.Trigger
	// Delay is After's duration; zero for every other trigger.
	Delay   time.Duration
}
```

<a name="Trigger"></a>
## type [Trigger](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/app/statemachine/facade_gen.go>)

Trigger says what fired a transition: a start, an event, a delay, a deadline or a guard.

```go
type Trigger = corestm.Trigger
```

Trigger is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/app/statemachine.Trigger`, declared as:

```go
type Trigger uint8
```

<a name="Trigger.String"></a>
### func \(Trigger\) [String](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/app/statemachine/trigger.go>)

```go
func (Trigger) String() string
```

String returns the trigger's name — "start", "event", "delay", "deadline" or "guard" — or "" for a value outside the set, which is how a caller tells a trigger from one that is not.
